abstract: Aberrant intracellular proteins triggered by various abnormalities, such as misfolding or mislocalization, are degraded by protein quality-control (PQC) systems. However, how extracellular PQC (ePQC) recognizes and eliminates cytosolic proteins -leaked and extracellularly mislocalized upon tissue injury- remains poorly understood. Here, we identify sortilin as a novel ePQC scavenger receptor that preferentially recognizes leaked, non-glycosylated cytosolic proteins in the extracellular space as abnormal and targets them for lysosomal degradation. Through hydrophobic interactions mediated by multiple hydrophobic patches on the sortilin surfaces, sortilin broadly engages diverse cytosolic substrates (e.g., hemoglobin), while discriminating against secreted proteins protected by hydrophilic glycans. Crucially, this clearance is driven by a hit-and-run shuttling mechanism: sortilin resides at the cell surface for only a few minutes, and this rapid cycling, combined with broad-spectrum recognition, enables the degradation of even low-affinity substrates. Together, these findings establish sortilin as an ePQC scavenger receptor for extracellularly mislocalized cytosolic proteins.
